title: Paris, Florence & Rome
intro: Five days in Paris over New Year's, three in Florence over Epiphany, and three in Rome. All three hotels are booked. The booking list at the end has every timed ticket and table to reserve.

days.label: Wed · Arrive in Paris
days.tagline: Land at 1 PM, then a whole afternoon in the Marais: falafel, leather and vintage shops, Notre-Dame lit up, and a rooftop nightcap.

blocks.title: Hôtel Lodge In Paris 13
blocks.text: Land at CDG at 1 PM. Taxi at the fixed airport fare to the Left Bank, about €65 and 50 minutes. Drop bags and go.
blocks.note: Booked: twin room, Dec 30 to Jan 4, check-in from 3 PM. A 3-star by Porte d'Ivry in the 13th, a 10-minute walk from Métro line 7. Line 7 runs to the Marais and the Louvre in about 25 minutes.

nearby.text: The Festival du Merveilleux runs Dec 26 to Jan 3 in a hall full of 1900s carousels you can actually ride. It is across the river from the hotel, open 10 AM to 6 PM, and tickets are about €23 with two rides included.
A real Paris gaming club ten minutes from the hotel, in Chinatown. Blackjack, poker, and Sic Bo, open 2 PM to 6 AM, 18+ with a passport.
A cheap rum bar on the Butte-aux-Cailles, a hilltop village of cobbled lanes in the 13th. Try the house-infused rums, then wander the lit streets.
Paris's first urban cable car opened in December 2025. Take Métro 8 to Pointe du Lac and ride 4.5 km over the suburbs for a normal bus ticket.

blocks.title: Late lunch on the Rue des Rosiers
blocks.text: The famous pita stuffed with falafel, fried eggplant, and tahini. Eat it standing on the street. The line moves fast.
blocks.note: Closed Friday evening and Saturday.

nearby.text: Buckwheat galettes and salted-butter caramel crêpes with Breton cider. Sit-down and calm.
Paris's oldest covered market, with Moroccan, Japanese, and Italian stalls at shared tables.
A French label known for slim leather jackets, a few doors from L'As du Fallafel. Mid-priced and open daily.
Christophe Adam's éclair shop on Rue Pavée. Glossy, inventive flavors like salted caramel and passion fruit.
A cramped, cheap vintage shop on Rue de Rivoli with racks of leather jackets. Open daily from 11 AM.

blocks.title: Place des Vosges and the Marais courtyards
blocks.text: Walk the arcades around the Place des Vosges, the oldest square in Paris. Then slip into the hidden cobbled courtyards of Village Saint-Paul, full of antique dealers.
blocks.note: Enter Village Saint-Paul through the arcades on Rue Saint-Paul or Rue Charlemagne.

nearby.text: If you want a museum, the free Paris history museum is two blocks away. Last entry around 5:15 PM.
A three-floor design and homeware store with a used-book café.
Jacques Genin makes the best caramels in Paris. Go upstairs for a millefeuille assembled to order and a thick hot chocolate.
Vintage sold by weight. Leather jackets go for about €30 a kilo, so a jacket can cost under €50.

blocks.title: Notre-Dame at dusk
blocks.text: Walk across to the islands and into the restored cathedral as the light fades. Entry is free.
blocks.note: Reserve a free timed slot on the cathedral's site to skip most of the line. It closes around 7 PM on weekdays. Stop at Berthillon on Île Saint-Louis for ice cream.

nearby.text: The island's classic ice cream maker. Salted caramel and wild strawberry.

blocks.title: Leather and vintage in the Marais
blocks.text: Walk back into the Marais and shop Rue de Rivoli and Rue des Rosiers. Try on jackets at The Kooples, then dig through the vintage racks at Free'P'Star.
blocks.note: Most Marais shops close around 7:30 or 8 PM. Both shops are a 15-minute walk from Chez Janou.

nearby.text: Vintage by the kilo, where a leather jacket can cost under €50.

blocks.title: Dinner at Chez Janou
blocks.text: A busy Provençal bistro near the Place des Vosges. Order the duck, and the chocolate mousse served from a giant bowl.
blocks.note: Reserve. Métro line 7 runs home from Pont Marie, a 10-minute walk away.

nearby.text: Steak and lamb grilled over a wood fire in a rustic Marais room.
A neighborhood bistro near Chez Janou with a well-loved grilled steak and frites. A good backup if Janou is full.
A buzzy oyster and cocktail bar on a Marais corner, five minutes from Chez Janou. Order oysters and the Rain Dog.
The archetypal Paris bistro. Steak au poivre, frites, and a Paris-Brest.
A modern bistro with Asian touches from two sisters, nearby.
A butcher shop that cooks your steak at a few counter seats. Pick an entrecôte or côte de bœuf from the case. No reservations.

blocks.title: Rooftop cocktails at Bonnie
blocks.text: Ride up the SO/ Paris tower for cocktails with a wide view over the Seine and the Marais. It is a 15-minute walk from Chez Janou.
blocks.note: The bar is open daily 4 PM to 2 AM. The club opens Wednesday to Saturday at 11 PM, so it runs on Dec 30 if you want to dance.

nearby.text: Oysters and cocktails on a Marais street corner.
A speakeasy hidden behind a pizzeria's freezer door.
A speakeasy hidden behind the freezer door of a pizzeria near Bastille. Walk straight through Da Vito and push the cold-room door.
A speakeasy behind a taqueria, a block away.
A loud, graffiti-covered bar that uses only French spirits. The cocktails are clever and fairly cheap for Paris.
One of the world's top cocktail bars, behind a small red door in the upper Marais.

days.label: Thu · New Year's Eve
days.tagline: The Louvre, the Tuileries, and the Opéra by day. Then champagne, a grand dinner, and midnight facing the Eiffel Tower.

blocks.title: Musée du Louvre
blocks.text: Go at opening and see the big three first: the Mona Lisa, the Winged Victory, and the Venus de Milo. Then the Napoleon III apartments.
blocks.note: Timed ticket required, about €32 for non-EU visitors. Closed Tuesdays and Jan 1, so today is the day.

nearby.text: François Pinault's contemporary art under a restored dome by Tadao Ando. A 10-minute walk east.
The oldest pâtisserie in Paris, open since 1730 on Rue Montorgueil. Get the baba au rhum, which they invented.
A huge vintage store near Les Halles with a big wall of leather jackets. Open Monday to Saturday from 10:30 AM.
A bar with free retro arcade cabinets near Les Halles. Play the old fighting and racing games with your drinks.

blocks.title: Hot chocolate at Angelina
blocks.text: Thick African hot chocolate and the Mont-Blanc chestnut pastry in a Belle Époque tearoom on the Rue de Rivoli.

nearby.text: A mosaic-floored 1820s covered arcade with old bookshops, behind the Palais-Royal.
A pretty pastry tearoom facing the Tuileries, a block from Angelina. Quieter, with excellent Paris-Brest and hot chocolate.
An old-school bistro by the Place des Victoires with a cheap entrecôte under a sprig of thyme. Mains are cheap for Paris.

blocks.title: The Tuileries and the Palais-Royal
blocks.text: Walk off the hot chocolate across the Tuileries, then cut through the Palais-Royal's arcades and striped columns on the way to the covered passages.

nearby.text: Monet's Water Lilies in two oval rooms at the end of the Tuileries. Skip it if the Louvre was enough. Book a slot if you go.
The original 1862 Ladurée tearoom on Rue Royale, five minutes from the Orangerie. Buy a box of macarons or sit for a Saint-Honoré.

blocks.title: The covered passages
blocks.text: Walk through two glass-roofed 19th-century arcades. Passage des Panoramas has old engravers and stamp dealers. Passage Jouffroy has toy shops and the wax museum.
blocks.note: Panoramas is open 6 AM to midnight and Jouffroy 7 AM to 9:30 PM. Galeries Lafayette is a 10-minute walk.

nearby.text: The wax museum at the mouth of Passage Jouffroy. Check its Dec 31 hours.
The 1911 bar where the Bloody Mary was born, between Galeries Lafayette and the passages.

blocks.title: Galeries Lafayette
blocks.text: See the giant Christmas tree under the stained-glass dome, then go up to the free rooftop terrace for the view.

nearby.text: The other great department store, next door to Galeries Lafayette. Its Art Nouveau glass dome and big men's store are worth a look.
Cédric Grolet's bakery sells famous trompe-l'œil fruit pastries and croissants. Open Wednesday to Sunday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with a line.

blocks.title: Champagne at Harry's Bar
blocks.text: The 1911 American bar a few minutes from the Opéra, where the French 75 was named. Start the night with one before dinner.
blocks.note: Usually open until 2 AM. No New Year's Eve ticketing has been announced, so arrive early for a seat.

nearby.text: A top-50 world cocktail bar behind an Italian restaurant by the Galerie Vivienne. It opens at 6 PM.

blocks.title: New Year's Eve dinner at Café de la Paix
blocks.text: The grand 1862 café facing the Opéra serves a Paris 1900 dinner on New Year's Eve. The terrace menu is the realistic pick.
blocks.note: Published for Dec 31, 2026: €120 on the covered terrace, or €445 with champagne in the main hall. Book on TheFork now. Leave by 10:30 PM for the Trocadéro.

nearby.text: A Marais bistro with a set menu of oysters or foie gras, then Charolais beef fillet or duck, then dessert. A champagne aperitif is included. Published for Dec 31, 2026: €96 per person. Book on OpenTable.

The gilded 1900 dining room above Gare de Lyon. It serves a set New Year's Eve menu in a room that feels like a party. The 2026 menu is not announced yet. Book as soon as it opens, since it sells out.

The cheap, historic bouillon on the Grands Boulevards keeps its normal menu on New Year's Eve. Expect about €25 a head without drinks. No special menu has been announced. It takes no reservations, so go early and expect a line.
A cheaper Art Nouveau bouillon with classic French dishes at low prices.

blocks.title: Midnight at the Trocadéro
blocks.text: Stand on the Trocadéro terrace facing the Eiffel Tower across the river. At midnight the tower sparkles, and the Arc fireworks pop up behind you. It is crowded and happy, but not a Times Square crush.
blocks.note: Métro line 9 from the Opéra to Trocadéro, about 15 minutes. In 2025 Iéna and Boissière stations shut at 4 PM and Passy at 9 PM, so use Trocadéro station and arrive by 11 PM. Bag checks, and no glass bottles. Transport was free from 5 PM Dec 31 to noon Jan 1.

nearby.text: A tearoom on the Place du Trocadéro itself. Get a hot chocolate or a glass of champagne before you take your spot. Usually open until about midnight. It gets very busy on Dec 31.
The Shangri-La's botanical cocktail bar is a few steps from the Trocadéro. Cocktails cost about €30. Usually open daily 6 PM to 2 AM. Ask ahead about a New Year's Eve booking or cover charge.

The gilded bridge has a clear side view of the Eiffel Tower sparkle. It is calmer than the Trocadéro and close to the Champs-Élysées south entrance. Concorde, Champs-Élysées–Clemenceau, and Tuileries stations closed at 4 PM in 2025. Walk in from Invalides.

The basilica steps look over the whole city. The mood is relaxed, with people popping bottles on the stairs. The Arc fireworks are far away from here and look small. Expect crowds on the steps and some loose firecrackers.

Skip unless you want the big crowd. The official show is on the Champs-Élysées. At 11:50 PM a light show is projected on the Arc de Triomphe, then fireworks start at midnight. This is the Times Square of Paris: a fenced avenue packed with hundreds of thousands of people from 7 PM, with bag checks. Étoile station closed at 2 PM in 2025. Go only if you want the big crowd.

blocks.title: After midnight along the Seine
blocks.text: Cross the Pont d'Iéna under the glowing tower, then walk the river east to the gilded Pont Alexandre III, about 30 minutes. The trains are packed until about 1 AM, so a late drink is the easy way to wait.
blocks.note: Métro line 7 home runs from Palais Royal, a taxi or a short Métro ride from the bridge. Expect surge prices on ride apps until 2 AM.

nearby.text: The famous speakeasy near Les Halles runs late on weekend and holiday nights. Usually open until 4 AM on Fridays and Saturdays. New Year's Eve may need a ticket or reservation.

Walk along the Seine to the Pont des Arts after midnight. In 2025 public transport was free from 5 PM on Dec 31 to noon on Jan 1. Expect packed trains near the Champs-Élysées until about 1 AM, when its stations reopen.
A smart gaming club on the Champs-Élysées with blackjack, poker, and punto banco. Usually open 1 PM to 6 AM, 18+ with a passport.

days.label: Fri · New Year's Day
days.tagline: A slow holiday on the Left Bank: Saint-Germain and the Luxembourg, then the Eiffel Tower at sunset and steak frites.

blocks.title: Late breakfast at Café de Flore
blocks.text: Omelettes and hot chocolate at the Saint-Germain café that stays open every day of the year.

nearby.text: Its neighbor and rival, with the same view of the church and the boulevard.

blocks.title: Jardin du Luxembourg
blocks.text: A winter walk past the palace, the Medici Fountain, and the bare chestnut alleys.

nearby.text: Delacroix's murals of Jacob wrestling the angel, in the first chapel on the right.

blocks.title: The Eiffel Tower at sunset
blocks.text: Walk under the tower, then cross to the Trocadéro. It sparkles for five minutes at the top of every hour after dark.
blocks.note: Going up is optional. If you want the summit, book online.

nearby.text: The classic full view of the tower from across the river.
A two-level iron bridge with a framed view of the tower.
A 1927 tearoom on the Place du Trocadéro, open every day. Order the hot chocolate in a silver pot with a dish of whipped cream.
The most ornate bridge in Paris, with gilded statues and old lamps. Walk it after dark with the Eiffel Tower in view.

blocks.title: Dinner at Le Relais de l'Entrecôte
blocks.text: One dish only: steak with a secret green sauce and endless frites. It opens every day, but check holiday hours.
blocks.note: No reservations. Get there early.

nearby.text: Paris's oldest café, open since 1686, with coq au vin and Napoleon's hat.
A dark, theatrical cocktail bar two streets from the Entrecôte. Usually open 8 PM to 2 AM.

days.label: Sat · Islands & Saint-Germain
days.tagline: Stained glass, bookshops, lunch, and shopping in Saint-Germain, then a Seine cruise, a bouillon, and a jazz cellar.

blocks.title: Sainte-Chapelle
blocks.text: Fifteen walls of 13th-century stained glass. Morning light is best.
blocks.note: Book a time slot. Expect an airport-style security line.

nearby.text: The medieval prison where Marie Antoinette was held. A combined ticket covers both.

blocks.title: Shakespeare and Company
blocks.text: The English-language bookshop facing Notre-Dame. Buy a book to get its stamp.

nearby.text: Foucault's pendulum and the crypt of Voltaire, Hugo, and Curie.
A tiny shop selling choux cream puffs in flavors like pistachio and salted caramel. A box of six is about €10.

blocks.title: Lunch at Le Comptoir du Relais
blocks.text: A tiny Saint-Germain bistro. At lunch it takes walk-ins for classic brasserie plates.

nearby.text: Pierre Hermé's macarons are the best in Paris. Try the Ispahan with rose, lychee, and raspberry.

blocks.title: Shopping in Saint-Germain
blocks.text: Walk down Rue du Bac to Le Bon Marché, the first department store in Paris, with its food hall next door. Stop at Deyrolle on the way, a taxidermy shop open since 1831.

nearby.text: Impressionists in a Beaux-Arts train station, ten minutes north. Go only if you want a museum today. Book a slot.

blocks.title: La Samaritaine
blocks.text: The restored Art Nouveau department store by the Pont Neuf. Look up at the glass roof and peacock fresco, and browse the leather and menswear floors.
blocks.note: Open daily 10 AM to 8 PM, including Sundays. The Seine cruise leaves a few minutes' walk away.

nearby.text: The leafy tip of the Île de la Cité, right by the cruise dock. It is lovely after dark.

blocks.title: Seine cruise at dusk
blocks.text: An hour-long boat ride from the tip of the Île de la Cité as the bridges light up.

blocks.title: Dinner at Bouillon Racine
blocks.text: A 1906 Art Nouveau dining room of mirrors and carved wood. Order the beef cheek or the duck confit, then the crème brûlée.
blocks.note: Reserve online. A 10-minute walk to the jazz cellar after.

blocks.title: Swing jazz at Le Caveau de la Huchette
blocks.text: A medieval cellar where locals swing-dance to live jazz every night. It appeared in La La Land, and anyone can join the dance floor.
blocks.note: Open nightly from about 9 PM, until about 4 AM on Saturdays. There is a cover charge at the door.

nearby.text: A dark, theatrical cocktail bar near the Entrecôte.
Walk the footbridge on the way, with the Louvre lit up on one side.

days.label: Sun · Versailles & Montmartre
days.tagline: Versailles on its free first Sunday, then Montmartre at night: the funicular, Sacré-Cœur, a bouillon, and a rooftop.

blocks.title: Palace of Versailles
blocks.text: RER C to Versailles Château Rive Gauche, about 40 minutes. See the Hall of Mirrors and the King's apartments first.
blocks.note: The palace is free on the first Sunday from November to March, and Jan 3 qualifies. You still must reserve a free timed slot. Arrive early.

blocks.title: Lunch at Ore
blocks.text: Alain Ducasse's café inside the palace. A nice lunch without leaving the grounds.
blocks.note: Reserve.

blocks.title: The Trianon and the Queen's Hamlet
blocks.text: Walk through the gardens to the Grand Trianon and Marie Antoinette's mock village. The fountains are off in winter.

blocks.title: Sacré-Cœur and Montmartre at night
blocks.text: Ride the funicular up from the bottom of the steps, then see the basilica lit up and the city below. Wander the Place du Tertre and down the Rue de l'Abreuvoir.

nearby.text: Renoir's old studio and gardens overlooking the last Montmartre vineyard.
A wall of 'I love you' in 250 languages.
A two-minute funicular up the hill to Sacré-Cœur. It costs one Métro ticket, and you must validate a new one at the gate.
A winner of the Paris best-baguette prize, just off Place des Abbesses. Grab a baguette tradition or a croissant. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.
A heated, covered rooftop bar with a view over Paris to the Eiffel Tower. No reservations, and cocktails start at 3:30 PM.

blocks.note: The basilica stays open until 10:30 PM. The funicular takes one Métro ticket.

blocks.title: Dinner at Bouillon Pigalle
blocks.text: A cheap, cheerful French canteen that opens every day of the year. Snails, duck confit, and profiteroles.
blocks.note: No reservations. Expect a short queue.

nearby.text: The original 1896 bouillon. Also open every day.

blocks.title: Nightcap on the Terrass'' rooftop
blocks.text: Walk ten minutes uphill from Pigalle to a heated rooftop bar with a view across all of Paris. Watch the Eiffel Tower sparkle on the hour.
blocks.note: Open to non-guests without a reservation. Check the Sunday closing time before you go.

days.label: Mon · Paris → Florence
days.tagline: Fly to Florence, then cross the Ponte Vecchio and climb to the city's best sunset.

blocks.title: Fly Paris → Florence
blocks.text: Direct flights from CDG or Orly to Florence take about 1 hour 50 minutes. Taxi from Florence airport to the center takes about 20 minutes.
blocks.note: Book the flight. The Uffizi and Accademia close on Mondays, so today is for walking.

blocks.title: Essence Hotel
blocks.text: A 15-minute taxi from the airport. Leave bags and go.
blocks.note: Booked: double or twin room with a view, Jan 4 to 7, check-in 2 to 7:30 PM. A remodeled guesthouse on one floor of a building on Piazza della Indipendenza. Reception closes in the evening, so get the door code at check-in. A 15-minute walk to the Duomo.

blocks.title: Piazza della Signoria and the Ponte Vecchio
blocks.text: Walk past the Palazzo Vecchio and its statues, then cross the jewelers' bridge into the Oltrarno.

nearby.text: A hole-in-the-wall since 1875 selling small panini and glasses of wine for a few euros. Eat standing on the street, since there are no tables. Closed Sundays and cash only.
A street cart on Piazza dei Cimatori selling lampredotto, slow-cooked cow stomach in a roll. Ask for it bagnato, with the bun dipped in broth, and green sauce on top.
A tiny lampredotto and tripe window near Dante's house, popular with locals. The lampredotto is stewed with tomato and onion, so it stays soft.
A guided tour of the hidden staircases inside Palazzo Vecchio, including Francesco I's secret study. Groups are about 12 people, so book a slot ahead.
A glove maker at the south end of the Ponte Vecchio since 1919. Every pair is made in its own workshop, lined in silk, cashmere, or wool. Closed Sundays.
An old gelateria a minute from the Signoria, open since 1939. Get the pistachio or the fior di latte.

blocks.title: Sunset at Piazzale Michelangelo
blocks.text: A 20-minute uphill walk to the view over the whole city. Sunset is about 5 PM in early January.

nearby.text: A Romanesque church just above, where monks sing Gregorian vespers in the early evening.
A free terraced garden just below Piazzale Michelangelo, with a small Japanese garden and bronze sculptures by Folon. It closes around 5 PM in winter, so go up through it.

blocks.title: Dinner at Trattoria Sostanza
blocks.text: A narrow 1869 trattoria famous for its butter chicken and artichoke tortino.
blocks.note: Reserve by phone. Long cash-only, so bring euros.

nearby.text: A cellar trattoria serving bistecca alla fiorentina since 1886.

blocks.title: Negroni nightcap on the Signoria
blocks.text: Walk 12 minutes from Sostanza to Gucci Giardino 25, a small cocktail bar facing Palazzo Vecchio. Order a Negroni, the drink Florence invented in 1919. Then walk home past the lit Duomo.
blocks.note: Book a table online. Open until about 1 AM.

nearby.text: Florence's oldest café, on Piazza della Repubblica and open until about midnight. A good spot for a late Negroni or a hot chocolate.
An antique carousel with gilded horses, run by the same family for over 100 years. It runs from about November to May, and adults can ride.

days.label: Tue · The dome & the market
days.tagline: Bomboloni, the climb up Brunelleschi's dome, the market, a leather jacket, and dinner at Cibrèo.

blocks.title: Bomboloni and cappuccino at Cucciolo
blocks.text: A slow start. A narrow bar known for bomboloni, Tuscan doughnuts filled to order with custard, chocolate, or jam. Grab one warm with a cappuccino.

blocks.title: Climb Brunelleschi's dome
blocks.text: 463 steps between the two shells of the dome, past the Last Judgment frescoes, to the lantern.
blocks.note: Book the Brunelleschi Pass with a timed dome slot weeks ahead. It also covers the baptistery, bell tower, and museum.

nearby.text: Michelangelo's David is five minutes north. Skip it unless you want a museum today, since the Uffizi is tomorrow. About an hour, book a slot.
Giotto's bell tower: 414 steps, and the best view of the dome itself.
The original baptistery doors and Michelangelo's late Pietà.
A historic café on the corner facing the Baptistery. Try the budino di riso, a small rice-pudding tart in buttery pastry.
An organic gelateria right on the Duomo square that makes its own cones. A good stop after the dome climb.

blocks.title: Lunch at Mercato Centrale
blocks.text: Downstairs, a lampredotto sandwich at Da Nerbone. Upstairs, fresh pasta and pizza counters.

nearby.text: A family trattoria behind the market, open at lunch only since 1953. Shared tables, no bookings, and a bistecca priced by weight. Closed Sundays and cash only.
A big trattoria on the market square, open from 11 AM to 11 PM every day. Order the ribollita or the pappardelle with wild boar.
A leather shop locals rate as fair, with jackets that can be altered or made to your measurements in a few days. Compare it with the San Lorenzo stalls next door before you buy anything there.
A tiny chapel covered in Gozzoli's frescoes of the Three Kings riding through Tuscany. It fits the Epiphany theme. Closed Wednesdays, so go today. Only a few visitors fit at a time.
A modern steakhouse on the Accademia's street, with a big list of Tuscan reds. Open for lunch and dinner every day. Book ahead.

blocks.title: Santa Maria Novella pharmacy
blocks.text: A 400-year-old apothecary of frescoed rooms selling perfumes and soaps made by monks' recipes.

nearby.text: The basilica next door, with Masaccio's Holy Trinity.

blocks.title: Santa Croce
blocks.text: The tombs of Michelangelo, Galileo, and Machiavelli, and Giotto's chapel frescoes.
blocks.note: Last entry around 5 PM.

nearby.text: One of Florence's oldest gelato shops, a block away.
A perfume workshop in a palazzo by Santa Croce, making scents by hand from raw essences. Ask to smell the Florentine iris.
A chocolate shop with a machine that keeps hot chocolate turning all day. Choose 65 or 75 percent, plain or with chili. Closed Sundays.
A pastry shop famous for bomboloni and cream-filled cornetti, with a constant line of locals. Closed Sundays.
An old pastry shop near the Sant'Ambrogio market. Budino di riso and sfogliatine come out of the oven around 4 PM.

blocks.title: Leather jacket at Scuola del Cuoio
blocks.text: A leather school founded after World War II in the old friars' rooms behind Santa Croce. You can watch artisans cut and stitch, and the jackets are made in-house. Prices are high, but the quality is real.
blocks.note: Closes around 6 PM, so go before the basilica if you want more time. Items it does not stock can be made to order and shipped. Florence's winter sales usually start in early January, so ask about discounts. Avoid jackets from San Lorenzo stalls: check for a vera pelle label, a stiff, thin hide, and pushy sellers.

nearby.text: A young Florentine brand that makes all its leather jackets in Italy. It can make a jacket in another color or size in about a week and ship it home.
A luxury outlet with Gucci, Prada, and Saint Laurent stores in the hills east of the city. The direct bus from near Santa Maria Novella takes under an hour each way, so it costs a half day.

blocks.title: Dinner at Cibrèo Trattoria
blocks.text: Fabio Picchi's Tuscan trattoria by the Sant'Ambrogio market. No pasta, but excellent soups and stews.
blocks.note: No reservations. Arrive at opening.

nearby.text: Candlelit Oltrarno wine bar and restaurant with modern Tuscan food.

blocks.title: Cocktails at Locale
blocks.text: A world-ranked cocktail bar in a 13th-century palazzo, five minutes from Cibrèo. Drinks use house-made infusions and are served in rooms with vaulted ceilings and old stone.
blocks.note: Open about 7:30 PM to 2 AM daily. Reserve a table for a weekday night.

nearby.text: An old standing wine bar behind the Duomo, on the walk home. Glasses of Chianti cost a few euros. Closed Mondays.

days.label: Wed · Epiphany
days.tagline: The Uffizi at opening, schiacciata for lunch, the Epiphany parade, and bistecca for dinner.

blocks.title: Uffizi Galleries
blocks.text: Botticelli's Birth of Venus and Primavera, Leonardo, and Caravaggio. Plan on three hours.
blocks.note: Book the first entry slot. It is a national holiday, so it will be busy later.

nearby.text: The raised passage the Medici used to walk from the Uffizi over the Ponte Vecchio to Palazzo Pitti. It needs a special Uffizi ticket with a timed slot, and it ends near the parade's start.
A café on the Signoria since 1872, known for thick winter hot chocolate. Sit inside, since the terrace prices are high.
A small gelateria behind the Uffizi. Try the chocolate with chili or the ricotta and fig.

blocks.title: Schiacciata at All'Antico Vinaio
blocks.text: Giant focaccia sandwiches with mortadella, pistachio cream, and stracciatella.

nearby.text: The upstairs food hall of the central market, with pasta, pizza, and wine counters.

blocks.title: Cavalcata dei Magi
blocks.text: The Epiphany parade. Hundreds in Renaissance costume ride from Palazzo Pitti across the river to the Duomo.
blocks.note: It usually starts around 2 PM. Confirm the time and route the week before.

nearby.text: The Medici's terraced gardens behind the palace, with grottoes and city views.

blocks.title: Santo Spirito and the Oltrarno
blocks.text: Wander the artisan workshops of the south bank and see Brunelleschi's last church.

nearby.text: A family bookbinder facing Palazzo Pitti since 1856, selling marbled paper, journals, and leather desk goods. Hours on the holiday may be short.
A family gelateria on Piazza Tasso, at the far end of San Frediano. The flavors change with the season.

blocks.title: Aperitivo at Le Volpi e l'Uva
blocks.text: A tiny wine bar by the Ponte Vecchio, pouring small Tuscan producers by the glass.

blocks.title: Via de' Tornabuoni and a Negroni at Giacosa
blocks.text: Walk up Florence's luxury street on the way to dinner, past the Ferragamo, Gucci, and Pucci flagships. Stop at Giacosa, the café where Count Negroni first asked for his drink in 1919.
blocks.note: Shops in the center usually open on Epiphany, but many close by 7:30 PM. Order the Negroni Giacosa.

nearby.text: Ferragamo's flagship fills a medieval palazzo at the river end of the street. The shoes are the reason to go.
A small cocktail bar near Buca Lapi that uses only Italian spirits and vermouths. A good spot for a pre-dinner drink.

blocks.title: Bistecca at Buca Lapi
blocks.text: A cellar under Palazzo Antinori since 1880. Share a bistecca alla fiorentina, served rare.
blocks.note: Reserve.

nearby.text: An Oltrarno trattoria known for pear and pecorino ravioli.
A loud, old trattoria with hams hanging from the ceiling and shared tables. It serves a big bistecca and closes on Mondays, so tonight works.

blocks.title: Over the river to Santo Spirito
blocks.text: Walk off the steak across Ponte Santa Trinita, which has the best night view of the Ponte Vecchio. Then head to Piazza Santo Spirito, the Oltrarno's main nightlife square. Volume is a bar inside an old hat-form workshop, with the old tools still on the walls.
blocks.note: Volume is open until about 2 AM. The walk back to the hotel takes about 25 minutes.

nearby.text: A hidden speakeasy behind an unmarked door, and Florence's first. Book ahead, since entry is by reservation only and you ring a bell to get in.
A small, well-loved cocktail bar in San Frediano with a short, changing menu. Tell the bartender what you like and let them choose.
A tiny wine bar with a few tables and a great list by the glass. Ask for a natural Tuscan red.
A bistro that reopened its old wine window. Knock on the little wooden hatch and get a glass handed out to the street. It pours in the evening only.
A gelateria at the foot of Ponte Santa Trinita, open late. Try the black sesame.
A gelateria by Ponte alla Carraia with big portions and low prices. Open late every night.

days.label: Thu · Florence → Rome
days.tagline: A fast train, then the historic center on foot: Roscioli, the Pantheon, Trevi, the Spanish Steps, Pincio at sunset, and Via dei Condotti.

blocks.title: Train Florence → Rome
blocks.text: Frecciarossa or Italo from Santa Maria Novella to Roma Termini, about 1 hour 35 minutes. Then a 20-minute taxi to the hotel.
blocks.note: Book ahead for the lowest fares.

blocks.title: Bloom Hotel Rome
blocks.text: Taxi from Termini, about 20 minutes. Leave bags, then taxi back to the center for lunch.
blocks.note: Booked: Jan 7 to 10. Has a 24-hour front desk and a buffet breakfast. In the Aurelio area, a 13-minute walk from St. Peter's Square and about 15 minutes by taxi from the Pantheon.

blocks.title: Lunch at Roscioli
blocks.text: A deli and restaurant with some of Rome's best carbonara and cacio e pepe, and a deep wine list.
blocks.note: Reserve.

nearby.text: The family bakery around the corner. Pizza bianca and pizza rossa by the slice.
Roscioli's own pastry bar, two minutes away. Get a maritozzo, a soft bun split and packed with whipped cream.
A tiny, unsigned Jewish bakery in the Ghetto, a 3-minute walk. Order the ricotta and sour cherry tart. Cash only, and it often sells out by afternoon. Closed Saturdays.
A Roman Jewish trattoria on the Ghetto's main street. January is artichoke season, so try the carciofi alla giudia, fried whole until the leaves crunch like chips. Closed Tuesdays.
A Sicilian pastry shop around the corner from Roscioli. They fill the cannoli to order with sheep's-milk ricotta.
A small Renaissance fountain in Piazza Mattei, with bronze boys pushing turtles into the basin. It takes two minutes and sits on the way to the Ghetto.

blocks.title: The Pantheon
blocks.text: A 1,900-year-old temple with a concrete dome and an open oculus. About 30 minutes.
blocks.note: Book the small entry ticket online.

nearby.text: A painted ceiling with a fake dome. Stand on the marble disc.
Espresso, or granita di caffè with whipped cream, at the bar.
A coffee bar from 1938, steps from the Pantheon. Order the gran caffè, a foamy, pre-sweetened espresso. Pay at the register first.
A 1920s glass-roofed arcade on Via del Corso, a 5-minute walk. It reopened in 2024 with about 15 shops under a stained-glass ceiling.

blocks.title: Trevi Fountain and the Spanish Steps
blocks.text: Toss a coin at Trevi, then walk ten minutes to the Spanish Steps as the light fades.
blocks.note: Access to the fountain basin is now managed and can queue. Go early or late.

nearby.text: Rome's classic gelateria since 1900.
A department store between Trevi and the Corso. The basement shows a stretch of the ancient Aqua Virgo aqueduct, and the top floor has a terrace over the rooftops.
Chapels decorated with the bones of about 3,700 friars, arranged into chandeliers and arches. It is 10 minutes up from Trevi on Via Veneto and takes about 40 minutes.

blocks.title: Sunset from the Pincio
blocks.text: Climb from the top of the Spanish Steps along the Viale Trinità dei Monti to the Pincio terrace. The sun sets over St. Peter's dome around 4:55 PM.

nearby.text: Bernini's marble sculptures and Caravaggios in a villa at the far end of the park. Entry is by 2-hour timed slot only, so book a 2 PM slot to fit it in. Reservation required. Book the 3 PM slot.
A small 1920s neighborhood of fairy-tale towers, frescoes, and a frog fountain, a 10-minute taxi from the Borghese. It is best in daylight, so go first if you have time.

blocks.title: Shopping from Via Margutta to Via dei Condotti
blocks.text: Walk down from the Pincio to Via Margutta, a quiet lane of art studios where Roman Holiday was filmed. Then cut over to Via dei Condotti, Rome's luxury street, with Gucci, Prada, Bulgari, and Valentino. It ends at the Spanish Steps.
blocks.note: Most shops stay open until 7:30 or 8 PM. Piazza Navona is a 15-minute walk from the Spanish Steps.

nearby.text: Rome's best-known tiramisù, sold in single boxes to eat on the street. Try the classic and the strawberry one.
A glove maker since 1960 with a tiny shop on Piazza di Spagna. Hundreds of colors of Italian leather gloves, fitted to your hand.

blocks.title: Piazza Navona at night
blocks.text: Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers, lit up, a 15-minute walk from the Spanish Steps.

nearby.text: The café that invented the tartufo, a ball of chocolate gelato with a cherry inside and a dark chocolate shell. Eat it at the bar for less than at a table.

blocks.title: Dinner at Armando al Pantheon
blocks.text: A family trattoria since 1961 serving Roman classics: gricia, oxtail, and artichokes.
blocks.note: Reserve weeks ahead. Closed Sundays.

nearby.text: One of Rome's first wine bars, with a long list and cheese and salumi plates.

blocks.title: Cocktails at Jerry Thomas Speakeasy
blocks.text: A 10-minute walk from dinner to an unmarked door on a dark lane. Inside is a tiny 1920s-style bar that started Rome's cocktail revival. Ask the bartender for something built on Italian amari.
blocks.note: Book a table on the website, which also gives you the door password. It opens at 9 PM. Bring cash for the small membership fee and the drinks.

nearby.text: A sleek cocktail lounge facing the 2,000-year-old columns of the Temple of Hadrian, lit up at night. Easier to walk into than Jerry Thomas.
A late-night gelateria near Navona. Get it dipped in chocolate and rolled in nuts.

days.label: Fri · The Vatican & Prati
days.tagline: A whole day around the Vatican: the Sistine Chapel at opening, St. Peter's and its dome, Prati shopping, and sunset at Castel Sant'Angelo.

blocks.title: Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel
blocks.text: The Raphael Rooms, the map gallery, and Michelangelo's ceiling. Plan on three hours.
blocks.note: Book the first timed entry on the official Vatican Museums site as soon as dates open. Resellers sell an earlier 7:30 AM entry with breakfast for about €119, which gets you in before the crowds. Shoulders and knees must be covered in the museums, the Sistine Chapel, and St. Peter's, or you can be turned away. Bring photo ID. No photos or talking in the Sistine Chapel. Tickets are single entry, so you cannot leave and come back.

nearby.text: A 1919 coffee roaster in Prati, a 10-minute walk from the museum entrance. Order the caffè al cioccolato, an espresso in a cup lined with melted dark chocolate. Opens at 7 AM.
A Prati pastry shop since the 1960s, long known as Antonini. Locals come for the cornetti at breakfast and the small cakes in the window.

blocks.title: St. Peter's Basilica and the dome climb
blocks.text: Michelangelo's Pietà and Bernini's canopy. Entry is free. Climb the dome for a view over the square.
blocks.note: A side door from the Sistine Chapel straight into St. Peter's is often limited to guided groups. If it is closed to you, walk back out and around to St. Peter's Square, about 15 minutes, and use the basilica's own security line. Climb the dome: 551 steps, or take the lift for the first 231 and climb the last 320. It costs about €10 to €15, opens around 7:30 or 8 AM, and closes at 5 PM in winter. The last stretch is a narrow, leaning spiral. St. Peter's can close at short notice for ceremonies. Check the day before.

nearby.text: A pedestrian lane of old houses, cafés, and religious-goods shops between St. Peter's and Castel Sant'Angelo. It runs beside the Passetto, the walled escape corridor the popes used.
A tiny counter near St. Peter's where they roll fresh pasta in front of you and serve it in minutes. A plate costs under €10. Try the cacio e pepe or the amatriciana.
The cannon on the Gianicolo fires a blank at exactly noon every day. The terrace is a 20-minute walk south of St. Peter's and has one of the widest views of the city.

blocks.title: Lunch at Bonci Pizzarium
blocks.text: Gabriele Bonci's pizza by the slice, sold by weight with toppings that change hourly. Standing room only.

nearby.text: Rome's largest covered market, open Monday to Saturday mornings.

blocks.title: Shopping on Via Cola di Rienzo
blocks.text: Prati's main shopping street, a 10-minute walk from Pizzarium. It is a long, wide avenue of Italian chains, shoe shops, and food stores where Romans actually shop. It ends near the Tiber, close to Castel Sant'Angelo.
blocks.note: Shops reopen after lunch by about 3:30 PM and stay open until 7:30 or 8 PM.

nearby.text: A food hall and coffee roaster on the street since the 1930s. Good for Italian coffee, chocolate, and gifts to take home.
A small gelateria a block off Cola di Rienzo. Fruit flavors are made with fresh fruit, and the pistachio is excellent.

blocks.title: Castel Sant'Angelo at sunset
blocks.text: Hadrian's tomb turned papal fortress. Go up to the terrace for sunset over St. Peter's, about 5 PM.

blocks.title: Via dei Coronari
blocks.text: Cross the angel bridge from Castel Sant'Angelo and walk Via dei Coronari, a quiet lane of antique shops and old palazzi. It ends near Piazza Navona.
blocks.note: Shops close around 7:30 PM. Walk back over the angel bridge to Prati for dinner, about 15 minutes.

nearby.text: Gelato made in the window, with flavors like white peach and lavender or ricotta and fig. It sits halfway down the street.

blocks.title: Dinner at Il Sorpasso
blocks.text: A buzzy Prati wine bar and kitchen with cured meats hanging over the counter. Order a plate of salumi and the Roman pastas.
blocks.note: Book ahead for Friday night. Emerald's cocktail bar is around the corner for after.

nearby.text: A small, salon-style cocktail bar 10 minutes from Castel Sant'Angelo. The Sazerac and the dirty martini get the most praise. Good for a drink after sunset.

days.label: Sat · Ancient Rome & Trastevere
days.tagline: The Colosseum and the Forum, lunch in Monti, the Aventine keyhole at sunset, and a last night in Trastevere.

blocks.title: Colosseum
blocks.text: Go at opening. The arena-floor ticket lets you stand where the gladiators did.
blocks.note: Book on the official Parco archeologico site. The ticket includes the Forum and Palatine.

blocks.title: Roman Forum and Palatine Hill
blocks.text: Walk the Via Sacra past the Senate house and temples, then climb the Palatine for the view over the Forum.

blocks.title: Lunch at Ai Tre Scalini
blocks.text: An ivy-covered wine bar in Monti with plates of cheese, salumi, and meatballs.

nearby.text: A weekend market of vintage clothes and local designers.
Gelato with odd, good flavors like basil, honey and walnut, or chocolate with tobacco. It opens around 1:30 PM, two minutes from lunch.
A big vintage shop on Monti's main shopping street. It is strong on leather jackets, boots, and bags at secondhand prices.
A pastry shop from 1916 that many Romans say makes the city's best maritozzo. It is a 10-minute walk east of Monti. Closed Tuesdays.

blocks.title: Mouth of Truth and the Aventine keyhole
blocks.text: Put a hand in the Mouth of Truth, then climb the Aventine. Peek through the Knights of Malta keyhole at St. Peter's dome, and watch the sunset from the Orange Garden next door.
blocks.note: A 10-minute taxi from Monti. The Orange Garden closes at dusk, about 5 PM. Then walk 20 minutes down and over the river to Trastevere.

nearby.text: The original trapizzino shop in Testaccio, a 15-minute walk down from the Aventine. A pocket of pizza dough stuffed with Roman stews like chicken cacciatore or oxtail.

blocks.title: Trastevere
blocks.text: Walk the ivy-covered lanes to the golden mosaics of Santa Maria in Trastevere.

nearby.text: A small Trastevere gelateria that makes everything from scratch. The pistachio and dark chocolate are the ones to get.
A Trastevere fry shop for supplì, fried rice balls with a string of molten mozzarella inside. Try the classic and the cacio e pepe one. Closed Sundays.
A family biscuit bakery with a huge old oven. Buy a bag of brutti ma buoni, crunchy hazelnut meringue cookies, for later. Closed Sundays.

blocks.title: Dinner at Da Enzo al 29
blocks.text: A tiny trattoria with some of the best carbonara and fried artichokes in Rome.
blocks.note: No reservations at dinner. Put your name down and wait with a drink.

nearby.text: Creative Neapolitan-style pizza, ranked among Italy's best.
A Trastevere aperitivo bar in a former garage, busy with locals.
Cacio e pepe tossed at the table, and Roman lamb. A local favorite since 1936. Reserve.

blocks.title: Trastevere bars and the Tiber at night
blocks.text: Start at Bar San Calisto, a scruffy local favorite where a big Peroni is about €2.50. Then walk five minutes to Ma Che Siete Venuti a Fà, a tiny pub with 16 Italian craft beers on tap. Finish on Ponte Sisto, a footbridge with St. Peter's dome lit up down the river.
blocks.note: At San Calisto, pay at the register first, then hand your receipt to the bartender. Ma Che Siete is open until 2 AM.

nearby.text: A small basement blues and jazz club in Trastevere since 1984. Shows usually start around 10:30 PM, so check the night's lineup.
A late-night pastry bar, a 10-minute taxi south, serving maritozzi until about midnight. A classic Roman end to a night out.
Worth a 15-minute taxi to Monti. Drink Kong is a dark, neon-lit bar with retro arcade games, and it ranks among the World's 50 Best Bars. Pick a drink with a high Kong Factor for the house style.
A hotel terrace bar looking straight at the lit-up Colosseum. Pricey, at about €25 a cocktail, but the view is hard to beat. Reserve ahead.

days.label: Sun · Depart Rome
days.tagline: Breakfast at the hotel, then the airport for the 10 AM departure.

blocks.title: Taxi to Fiumicino
blocks.text: Taxi from the hotel to Fiumicino, about 30 minutes. The €55 fixed fare covers only the area inside the old city walls, so the meter may run. Be at the airport two hours before a 10 AM international flight.

reservations.status: Booked: Hôtel Lodge In Paris 13, Essence Hotel in Florence, and Bloom Hotel Rome.

Brunelleschi Pass with dome slot
reservations.status: Not booked. Sells out weeks ahead.

reservations.name: Armando al Pantheon
reservations.status: Not booked. Books up weeks ahead.

practical.title: Paris
practical.text: The hotel is at Porte d'Ivry in the 13th. Métro line 7 reaches the Marais and the Louvre in about 25 minutes. A Navigo Easy card or a phone wallet works on every line. Many shops and restaurants close on Jan 1.

practical.title: Florence
practical.text: Everything is walkable from the hotel on Piazza della Indipendenza: 15 minutes to the Duomo and 12 to the station. Jan 6 is a national holiday: museums open, some shops close.

practical.title: Rome
practical.text: The hotel is a 13-minute walk from St. Peter's. Take taxis to the center, the Colosseum, the Borghese, and Testaccio. Leave the hotel by 7:30 AM on Jan 10 for a 10 AM flight.

practical.title: Weather
practical.text: Expect highs around 45°F in Paris and the low 50s°F in Florence and Rome. Bring a warm coat and good walking shoes.
